tickerText: [TENNIS] Davis Cup qualifying closes with Spain, Great Britain and Alexander Zverev's Germany joining Czechia, South Korea, Austria and Canada in November's Final 8 in Bologna while the United States misses the knockout stage for a second straight year • [SQUASH] Monday's PSA rankings confirm Amina Orfi as the youngest women's world No. 1 after her Qatar Classic five-set win over Hania El Hammamy, with Mostafa Asal's sweep of Victor Crouin giving him every current major title • [BADMINTON] India's women are into the Asian Games quarterfinals after PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda and Tanvi Sharma blanked Kazakhstan 3-0 as the men's team opens round-of-16 play versus Bangladesh on Monday in Ichinomiya • [PICKLEBALL] Championship Sunday at the Veolia Arizona Open crowns Anna Leigh Waters over Kate Fahey, Chris Haworth over Hunter Johnson, and doubles titles for Waters/Johns, Rohrabacher/Todd and Staksrud/Johns in Mesa • [TABLE TENNIS] Dang Qiu rallies past Alexis Lebrun 4-2 to win the WTT Star Contender Astana while India's women stay unbeaten at the Asian Games but the men fall 3-1 to Iran before Monday group finales versus Pakistan

newsItems.title: Final Eight Field Complete
newsItems.excerpt: Spain, Great Britain and Germany wrapped Davis Cup qualifying on Sept. 20 with 3-0 wins over Chile, Ecuador and Croatia as Alexander Zverev sealed Germany's spot and the November Final 8 lineup in Bologna is set.

newsItems.title: India Women Into QFs
newsItems.excerpt: PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda and Tanvi Sharma swept Kazakhstan 3-0 on Sept. 20 to send India's women's badminton team into an Asian Games quarterfinal against Japan on Tuesday in Ichinomiya.

newsItems.title: Arizona Open Crowns Set
newsItems.excerpt: Anna Leigh Waters and Chris Haworth took singles titles at the Veolia Arizona Open on Sept. 20 in Mesa, with Waters/Johns, Rohrabacher/Todd and Staksrud/Johns winning doubles on the $1.06M PPA Championship Sunday.

newsItems.title: Qiu Wins Astana; Iran Stuns India
newsItems.excerpt: Dang Qiu beat Alexis Lebrun 4-2 on Sept. 20 to win the WTT Star Contender Astana, while India's women's table tennis team stayed perfect in Asian Games group play and the men were upset 3-1 by Iran.
